criteria.criterion: Provide bounded setup/start/status/stop commands for an owned durable development cluster outside artifacts; deny TCP listening, protect socket/data permissions, and never replace existing data or stop an unrelated process.
criteria.procedure: Execute actual candidate lifecycle and isolated safe-refusal tests in e. Launch two identical-binary PostgreSQL servers in the same second, substitute suffix PID, redirect readiness SQL to wrong server, mutate PID file exactly at pg_ctl signal boundary, test symlinked log/ancestor, stale dummy/malformed PID/socket, missing live PID, foreign owner, unsafe mode, and stalled readiness tools with child cleanup.
criteria.expected: Only the exact owned answering server may report ready or be stopped; errors are bounded and preserve other processes/data; private Unix socket and safe modes remain.
criteria.observed: 53 first-phase and 14 timeout-phase command records pass. Real PIDs 22471 and 22472 shared epoch 1790796747. Prefix substitution and wrong SQL backend refuse start/status/stop, leaving both servers live. PID-file race changed 22471 to 22472, but command was pg_ctl kill INT 22471; 22472 remained ready. Symlink log/ancestor refuse all four lifecycle commands; sentinel unchanged. Dummy received no signal. Missing-PID live server, stale socket, malformed PID, foreign owner and unsafe mode refuse. pg_isready/psql stalls returned errors in 10.284/10.778 seconds including prechecks/cleanup; injected parent and child PIDs were gone. No owned TCP listener. Durable data/socket directories are 0700. All evaluator-owned processes finally stopped.

criteria.criterion: Use real psql transactions to verify version, rollback/commit, restart persistence, parameter-safe diagnostic output and Pg readiness; preserve fsync/full_page_writes/synchronous_commit and explicit configured connection/process limits.
criteria.procedure: Use real psql -X fixed SQL for version and limits, rolled-back table absence, committed row, graceful stop/restart and persistence; observe readiness/private socket and use credential-looking environment sentinel to check output safety.
criteria.expected: Version 18.6; rollback leaves no table, committed data survives restart; sync safety and selected connection/worker bounds remain on; output excludes environment secrets.
criteria.observed: Actual PostgreSQL 18.6 returned max_connections 16, worker/parallel/gather/autovacuum limits 8/8/2/3, fsync/full_page_writes/synchronous_commit on, empty listen_addresses and inet_server_addr null. Rolled-back table absent; committed 186 survived graceful restart. Readiness recovered after timeout injection; output omitted sentinel. This establishes local development transaction/restart behavior, not disaster recovery or game schemas.
